# Catalog (/docs/corpus/catalog)

**What it is.** The hand-written source of every entry: what it is for, where its ledger comes from, and the facts to check. A compiler turns it into the entry.

**Why it matters.** Nobody edits the corpus by hand, and the compiler refuses any fact that doesn't hold, so a typo can't become a wrong answer.

Nobody edits `entries/` by hand. Each entry starts as a **catalog file**, `catalog/<id>.json`. It says what the entry is for, where its ledger comes from, and the facts a correct reader must find, written relative to the transaction the entry is about. The compiler, `tools/build.mjs`, turns it into `entries/<id>/` for every variant.

<Steps>
<Step>

### Write the intent

A catalog file carries:
- the id, title and pattern;
- the CAPs, and the hazards with their placement;
- the source: a recipe lane and step, or a mined ledger;
- the variants to build, such as `p30-mainnet`, `p28-testnet` or `p30-mainnet-galexie`, and optionally mined variants beside the generated ones;
- the focus: an operation of the step's transaction, or `{"ledger": true}` when the entry is about the ledger itself. A mined entry names its transaction by hash; the compiler never picks one;
- the facts.

</Step>
<Step>

### Compile it

```bash
make build                     # every catalog file (minutes)
node tools/build.mjs [id ...]  # only these entries
```

The compiler takes the ledger bytes from a fresh [`make generate`](/docs/tools/generate) run (or from [`mined/`](/docs/corpus/mined)) and finds the focus transaction. It resolves every fact into an exact JSON Pointer for that variant, and records size, sha256, provenance and change-order data. It needs the runs of `make generate`, for the base P30 mainnet variants also those of [`make order-scan`](/docs/tools/order-scan) (it ships the most frequent byte ordering), and the native reader (`make native`). A fact that doesn't hold fails the build, and so does a variant whose focus doesn't match the catalog's (a transaction where the catalog says ledger, or none where it names one): intent and outcome must agree before an entry exists.

</Step>
<Step>

### Check it

[`make verify`](/docs/tools/verify) and [`make oracle`](/docs/tools/oracle) check the built entries like any other. [`make novelty`](/docs/tools/novelty) then fails if the new entry adds nothing another entry doesn't already hold.

</Step>
</Steps>

## Fact addresses

A fact names where it looks with `at`. The compiler resolves that address per variant, so one catalog file serves every protocol, network and flag profile.

| `at` | Resolves to |
|---|---|
| `tx.result` | the focus transaction's result |
| `tx.result_pair` | the result pair (hash and result) |
| `tx.fee_charged` | the fee charged |
| `tx.envelope` | the envelope in the transaction set, in any phase, stage or cluster |
| `tx.meta` | the transaction's meta |
| `tx.fee_processing`, `tx.post_apply_fee` | the fee and post-apply fee changes |
| `op.meta`, `op.changes`, `op.events` | the focus operation inside the meta |
| `ledger` | the whole ledger: header, upgrades, evicted keys |

A value may be `{"$manifest": "contracts.kit2.CA1"}`. It is then read from the run's own manifest, so a fact holds on every network even though contract ids differ by passphrase.

<Callout title="Authoring aid">`node tools/inspect.mjs <lane> <step> [variant]` reads a `make generate` run and prints the focus transaction's result and fee, and for each operation the kinds of its changes and its events.</Callout>


# A payment of 9.5e15 stroops, above 2^53 (/docs/corpus/entries/amount-payment-above-2-pow-53)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (pre-cap):

- H-B3: PaymentOp.amount above 2^53 stroops

## The shape

An amount above 2^53 cannot be held exactly by a double: JavaScript numbers and float JSON parsers round it.

## Variants

| Variant | Protocol | Network | Source | Size | sha256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`p30-mainnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/amount.payment-above-2-pow-53/p30-mainnet-generated.xdr) | P30 | mainnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0 | 2,668 B | `7df1ef2e592b927cf29f6dbb0e47b7ab6b7fe557a88e9c273f17695b68d236b2` |
| [`p30-testnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/amount.payment-above-2-pow-53/p30-testnet-generated.xdr) | P30 | testnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0 | 2,668 B | `8e87f16dfff28e364e3d0f32de7ae3c9008ea322d0c5bfb497a3bbcd02b69ffd` |

## What a correct reader returns

| A correct reader finds | Value | Backed by |
|---|---|---|
| The amount is 9500000000000000 stroops. | `9500000000000000` | construction, snapshot, core, walker |
| Operation 0 succeeds. | `success` | snapshot, core, walker |

## Check it yourself


# A pool whose two issuers sort one way as strkeys and the other as bytes (/docs/corpus/entries/asset-order-pool-issuers-text-vs-bytes)

# A valid v1 create-contract authorization whose signature covers bytes it does not contain (/docs/corpus/entries/auth-create-contract-v1-signature-covers-v2-rendering)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (CAP-0046, CAP-0058):

- H-B16: a valid v1 create authorization: its signature covers the V2 rendering
- H-D5: HOST_FUNCTION_TYPE_CREATE_CONTRACT (v1) with address-credential auth
- H-F9: SorobanTransactionMetaExt v0 under the bare flag profile (no EMIT_SOROBAN_TRANSACTION_META_EXT_V1), v1 under base

## The shape

The same v1 create, its auth entry still carrying SOROBAN_AUTHORIZED_FUNCTION_TYPE_CREATE_CONTRACT_HOST_FN, but signed over the CREATE_CONTRACT_V2_HOST_FN rendering (empty constructor arguments) the host hashes: the contract is created. A verifier that recomputes the payload from the entry's bytes rejects a signature core accepted. Under the bare flag profile (no EMIT_SOROBAN_TRANSACTION_META_EXT_V1) the same call writes Soroban meta extension v0, without the fee breakdown base writes in v1. By design since protocol 22 (one valid payload per action; github.com/orgs/stellar/discussions/1501). tools/auth-payload-check.mjs re-checks the signatures with hand-encoded preimages.

# A v1 create-contract authorization signed over its own bytes fails verification (/docs/corpus/entries/auth-create-contract-v1-signed-over-own-bytes)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (CAP-0046, CAP-0058):

- H-B16: a v1 create authorization signed over its own bytes: verification fails

## The shape

HOST_FUNCTION_TYPE_CREATE_CONTRACT authorized by address credentials, root SOROBAN_AUTHORIZED_FUNCTION_TYPE_CREATE_CONTRACT_HOST_FN, signed over the entry's own bytes, as js-stellar-base's authorizeEntry signs it. The host reads the arm into its V2 form and hashes the signature payload from the V2 rendering (soroban-env-host auth.rs), so ed25519 verification fails and the call traps. This is by design since protocol 22: the host keeps one valid payload per action (github.com/orgs/stellar/discussions/1501). Transactions built through RPC simulation carry the V2 payload; offline signers must sign the V2 rendering.

# A forged address signature: the host fails ed25519 verification with an SCError of type crypto (/docs/corpus/entries/auth-forged-signature-crypto-error)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (CAP-0046):

- H-A7: an auth entry naming alice whose signature fails verification; alice authorized nothing
- H-C6: SCError.SCE_CRYPTO (invalid_input) in diagnostic events

## The shape

bob submits a call carrying an auth entry for alice whose signature covers another nonce. The host verifies it with ed25519 and fails with Error(Crypto, InvalidInput), then escalates to an auth error and the call traps. alice authorized nothing, yet her address sits in the transaction. Readers that index auth-entry addresses as participants, or decode SCError as host error types only, both go wrong.

# The deepest authorization tree core applies: 245 invocations; the WASM decoder rejects it (/docs/corpus/entries/auth-tree-depth-245-max)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (CAP-0046):

- H-B7: auth tree 245 nodes deep, the maximum that applies
- H-B13: a valid ledger the WASM decoder rejects (depth limit exceeded)
- H-A7: auth entries name an address the meta never touches

## The shape

One source-credential entry whose root invocation carries a chain of 244 never-called sub-invocations: 245 nodes, the deepest that applies at P30 (246 traps). The kits[1] contract appears 244 times in the auth and never in the meta. @stellar/stellar-xdr-json 30.0.0 (WASM) cannot decode this ledger; native rs-stellar-xdr can.

## Variants

# An offer match in a protocol-12 result decodes as ClaimOfferAtomV0: the seller is a raw ed25519 key (/docs/corpus/entries/backfill-claim-atom-v0-p12)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (CAP-0038):

- H-F8: ClaimAtom.CLAIM_ATOM_TYPE_V0 in a P12 result: the seller as raw ed25519, not an AccountID
- H-C7: an offer claim recorded as ClaimOfferAtomV0 (pre-P18 result bytes)

## The shape

Before protocol 18 an offer claim was a ClaimOfferAtom whose seller was an AccountID. CAP-0038 turned it into the ClaimAtom union and kept old bytes readable: the AccountID discriminant (0) now reads as CLAIM_ATOM_TYPE_V0, and the seller as a bare 32-byte ed25519 key (Stellar-transaction.x, "ClaimOfferAtomV0 is a ClaimOfferAtom with the AccountID discriminant stripped"). Old results in SDF's lake still carry it. Readers that only handle ORDER_BOOK and LIQUIDITY_POOL claim atoms, or that print the seller without converting it to a G address, fail on every pre-P18 trade.

## Variants

| Variant | Protocol | Network | Source | Size | sha256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`p12-mainnet-mined-l26588352`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/backfill.claim-atom-v0-p12/p12-mainnet-mined-l26588352.xdr.zst) | P12 | mainnet passphrase | mined from history | 887,884 B | `039ba91a4dfd229cbbc58204ce16afed91eb066f4b88219b7d1932f08359b584` |

## What a correct reader returns

| A correct reader finds | Value | Backed by |
|---|---|---|
| The claimed offer's seller is a raw ed25519 key in a V0 claim atom. | `ad0713a07a84a069367932edf2b6155c69aed69446e564168ab8fcd78d728785` | snapshot, core, walker |
| The claimed offer is offer 127478113. | `127478113` | snapshot, core, walker |

# CREATE_ACCOUNT: the new account appears as a CREATED entry and as a CAP-0067 transfer event (/docs/corpus/entries/event-classic-create-account-transfer)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (pre-cap, CAP-0067):

- H-E1: CreateAccountOp emits a CAP-0067 transfer event of native XLM to the new account

## The shape

Two CREATE_ACCOUNT operations in one transaction, each funding a new account with 1000 XLM. Each operation's meta holds the funder's state and update and the new account as a created entry, and, since CAP-0067, a transfer event of native XLM from the funder to the new account. Readers that count transfer events as payments double-count account funding; readers that only watch payment operations miss it.

## Variants

| Variant | Protocol | Network | Source | Size | sha256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`p30-mainnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/event.classic.create-account-transfer/p30-mainnet-generated.xdr) | P30 | mainnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0 | 2,740 B | `d386894f0344ae5edff097b5e10a0852027d743d23c79c59c5020d6c4a3b37c0` |
| [`p30-testnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/event.classic.create-account-transfer/p30-testnet-generated.xdr) | P30 | testnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0 | 2,740 B | `6479efb2b018cf3bcb6d5d6d6aab32ac6a02bc3eb0b4b106420f66100ad7659b` |

## What a correct reader returns

| A correct reader finds | Value | Backed by |
|---|---|---|
| Operation 0 succeeds. | `success` | snapshot, core, walker |

# ACCOUNT_MERGE fails with ACCOUNT_MERGE_DEST_FULL (/docs/corpus/entries/failure-account-merge-dest-full)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (pre-cap):

- H-C1: OperationResult.account_merge.dest_full in a closed ledger
- H-C11: merge into an account with no room below i64::MAX
- H-C17: native buying liabilities near i64::MAX
- H-B3: an account balance plus buying liabilities near i64::MAX

## The shape

A transaction whose ACCOUNT_MERGE operation fails at apply is still written into the closed ledger: its fee is charged, its sequence number is consumed, and nothing it did is kept. The result carries the operation's code (dest_full). The destination sells 429.4967297 NRV at 2147483647 XLM each: native buying liabilities of 2^63 - 2147483649 stroops, which leave it about 164 XLM of room below i64::MAX (TransactionUtils.cpp, addBalance). The 300 XLM merged in does not fit.

## The shape

A transaction whose ACCOUNT_MERGE operation fails at apply is still written into the closed ledger: its fee is charged, its sequence number is consumed, and none of its operations change state. The result carries the operation's result code (is_sponsor). # ACCOUNT_MERGE fails with ACCOUNT_MERGE_SEQNUM_TOO_FAR (/docs/corpus/entries/failure-account-merge-seqnum-too-far)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (pre-cap):

- H-C1: OperationResult.account_merge.seqnum_too_far in a closed ledger
- H-C11: merge after a bump past the ledger's starting sequence

## The shape

A transaction whose ACCOUNT_MERGE operation fails at apply is still written into the closed ledger: its fee is charged, its sequence number is consumed, and nothing it did is kept. The result carries the operation's code (seqnum_too_far). Operation 0 bumps the sequence number past this ledger's starting sequence (ledger << 32); merging could let the account be recreated with a lower number, so core refuses (MergeOpFrame.cpp, isSeqnumTooFar). Operation 0 reports success in the failed transaction.

# CLAWBACK_CLAIMABLE_BALANCE fails with CLAWBACK_CLAIMABLE_BALANCE_DOES_NOT_EXIST (/docs/corpus/entries/failure-clawback-claimable-balance-does-not-exist)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (CAP-0035):

- H-C1: OperationResult.clawback_claimable_balance.does_not_exist in a closed ledger

## The shape

A transaction whose CLAWBACK_CLAIMABLE_BALANCE operation fails at apply is still written into the closed ledger: its fee is charged, its sequence number is consumed, and none of its operations change state. The result carries the operation's result code (does_not_exist). Readers that skip failed transactions lose the fee and sequence change; readers that assume a failed transaction changed something record effects that never happened.

# A failed 14-operation offer transaction with two failure codes and twelve successes that changed nothing (/docs/corpus/entries/failure-manage-offer-fourteen-ops-two-codes-p12)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (pre-cap):

- H-C1: two failure codes (not_found at op 4, underfunded at op 13) in one failed tx; twelve other ops report success

## The shape

One transaction manages 14 offers. Operation 4 fails with not_found and operation 13 with underfunded; the other twelve report success, some with the offer deleted. The transaction failed, so none of it happened: the meta has no operation changes. Each operation still has its own result, including results evaluated after the first failure. Readers that take the first failing code as the only one, or that apply "success" results of a failed transaction, get both wrong.

- H-C1: OperationResult.manage_sell_offer.buy_not_authorized in a closed ledger
- H-C10: offer buying into an unauthorized trustline

## The shape

A transaction whose MANAGE_SELL_OFFER operation fails at apply is still written into the closed ledger: its fee is charged, its sequence number is consumed, and nothing it did is kept. The result carries the operation's code (buy_not_authorized). Buying ARQ into an unauthorized trustline.

| Variant | Protocol | Network | Source | Size | sha256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`p30-mainnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/failure.manage-sell-offer.buy-not-authorized/p30-mainnet-generated.xdr) | P30 | mainnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0 | 12,352 B | `5d1b0b6d6130f05dcaa137746352b2b85ff8f9af07028159c0c7058e7df75462` |
| [`p30-testnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/failure.manage-sell-offer.buy-not-authorized/p30-testnet-generated.xdr) | P30 | testnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0 | 12,352 B | `6958b55e5ea2071afe52b428d76c8abb5b6b2ed3cc0d4c36ece545cb59cdaf6b` |

# MANAGE_SELL_OFFER fails with MANAGE_SELL_OFFER_CROSS_SELF (/docs/corpus/entries/failure-manage-sell-offer-cross-self)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (pre-cap):

- H-C1: OperationResult.manage_sell_offer.cross_self in a closed ledger

## The shape

A transaction whose MANAGE_SELL_OFFER operation fails at apply is still written into the closed ledger: its fee is charged, its sequence number is consumed, and none of its operations change state. The result carries the operation's result code (cross_self). Readers that skip failed transactions lose the fee and sequence change; readers that assume a failed transaction changed something record effects that never happened.

# An offer that would cross 1001 offers fails with opEXCEEDED_WORK_LIMIT (/docs/corpus/entries/failure-op-exceeded-work-limit)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (pre-cap):

- H-C1: OperationResult.opEXCEEDED_WORK_LIMIT in a closed ledger
- H-C7: a buy offer that would cross 1001 offers

## The shape

One operation may cross at most 1000 offers (MAX_OFFERS_TO_CROSS, TransactionUtils.cpp). 1001 one-stroop WRK offers sit at one price; a buy offer for 1001 stroops would cross them all. The operation fails at the operation level, with no inner result of its type, and nothing crosses. Readers that expect every failed operation to carry an operation-specific code meet a bare opEXCEEDED_WORK_LIMIT.

## Variants

| Variant | Protocol | Network | Source | Size | sha256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`p30-mainnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/failure.op.exceeded-work-limit/p30-mainnet-generated.xdr) | P30 | mainnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0 | 14,368 B | `9d41b66de6ab14a2246e753d0ec5690ec523f108a5deff88c66a65ccd3e836d7` |
| [`p30-testnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/failure.op.exceeded-work-limit/p30-testnet-generated.xdr) | P30 | testnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0 | 14,368 B | `5f41a5a8623e1a1987a8a593e1bc7522cb1559af8c12b40958c6441a73787f13` |

## What a correct reader returns

# PATH_PAYMENT_STRICT_RECEIVE fails with PATH_PAYMENT_STRICT_RECEIVE_NO_DESTINATION (/docs/corpus/entries/failure-path-payment-strict-receive-no-destination)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (pre-cap):

- H-C1: OperationResult.path_payment_strict_receive.no_destination in a closed ledger

## The shape

A transaction whose PATH_PAYMENT_STRICT_RECEIVE operation fails at apply is still written into the closed ledger: its fee is charged, its sequence number is consumed, and none of its operations change state. The result carries the operation's result code (no_destination). Readers that skip failed transactions lose the fee and sequence change; readers that assume a failed transaction changed something record effects that never happened.

- H-C1: OperationResult.path_payment_strict_send.no_trust in a closed ledger

## The shape

A transaction whose PATH_PAYMENT_STRICT_SEND operation fails at apply is still written into the closed ledger: its fee is charged, its sequence number is consumed, and none of its operations change state. - H-C2: txFEE_BUMP_INNER_FAILED with a four-op inner result on mainnet

## The shape

A fee bump whose inner transaction is a sponsorship sandwich: begin sponsoring, remove one signer, add another, end sponsoring. # Apply order is not transaction-set order, and differs by network and protocol (/docs/corpus/entries/ledger-apply-order-differs-from-set-order)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (CAP-0063):

- H-C12: tx_processing order differs from tx_set order; classic phase before Soroban phase

## The shape

The transaction set lists transactions in phases sorted by hash; core applies the classic phase first, then the Soroban phase, each in an order shuffled by the hash of the whole set (TxSetFrame.cpp ApplyTxSorter). The same recipe gives a different apply order on each network and protocol. Readers that number transactions by their position in the set, or assume one order, misattribute results.

## Variants

| Variant | Protocol | Network | Source | Size | sha256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`p30-mainnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/ledger.apply-order-differs-from-set-order/p30-mainnet-generated.xdr) | P30 | mainnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0 | 17,236 B | `dbc26aa0d75267052a7b0ff3a399e6a5f1bd708bf51da7b88e10fce8e646ba9b` |
| [`p28-mainnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/ledger.apply-order-differs-from-set-order/p28-mainnet-generated.xdr) | P28 | mainnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0 | 17,228 B | `b464fb610c5dc4338e51264688075287b17489787054fc0a9a3ed48926be972c` |
| [`p30-testnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/ledger.apply-order-differs-from-set-order/p30-testnet-generated.xdr) | P30 | testnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0 | 17,132 B | `93d7ae80867e77f226d47e6e0b9ffda64102deea242ce75547630c1b054069d4` |

# One payment with a muxed transaction source, operation source and destination (/docs/corpus/entries/muxed-payment-every-position)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (CAP-0027):

- H-A1: Transaction.sourceAccount, Operation.sourceAccount and PaymentOp.destination as MuxedAccount
- H-A2: muxed IDs 1, 2^63 (above int64 max) and 2^64-1

## The shape

A payment where the transaction source, the operation source and the destination are all muxed accounts (M…), with IDs 1, 2^64-1 and 2^63. Each M address is a base account plus a 64-bit ID: the ID must be kept, and balances belong to the base account. Readers that store the M string as the account, or drop the ID, misattribute or lose the payment.

## Variants

| Variant | Protocol | Network | Source | Size | sha256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`p30-mainnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/muxed.payment.every-position/p30-mainnet-generated.xdr) | P30 | mainnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0 | 2,456 B | `fd9d0c246bf3504336ce6c6d6ce1ca8506d76fba4983ffa85ec2d63e49bfda23` |

| The operation source is alice muxed with ID 2^64-1. | `MBQXLZZTGUKRRRYDQNQOMKWL7DN3PGIBPNBIHDIO5KFPPPIFAHHQJ7777777777775YC2` | construction, snapshot, core, walker |

# An operation whose source signer was removed earlier in the ledger fails opBAD_AUTH (/docs/corpus/entries/op-apply-time-bad-auth)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (CAP-0046):

- H-C16: OperationResult.opBAD_AUTH in a closed ledger: operation-source signer removed earlier in the ledger

## The shape

Core applies a ledger's classic phase before its Soroban phase and re-checks the source account, sequence number, signatures and sequence-age preconditions at apply (TransactionFrame::commonValid; OperationFrame::checkSignature with forApply). Here a classic transaction earlier in the same ledger removes the key that signed for this transaction's operation source, so the transaction fails with txFAILED and the operation result opBAD_AUTH, while the transaction-level signature is still valid.

## Variants

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| [`p28-mainnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/op.apply-time.bad-auth/p28-mainnet-generated.xdr) | P28 | mainnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0 | 17,228 B | `b464fb610c5dc4338e51264688075287b17489787054fc0a9a3ed48926be972c` |
| [`p30-testnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/op.apply-time.bad-auth/p30-testnet-generated.xdr) | P30 | testnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0 | 17,132 B | `93d7ae80867e77f226d47e6e0b9ffda64102deea242ce75547630c1b054069d4` |

# An operation whose source account was merged earlier in the ledger fails opNO_ACCOUNT (/docs/corpus/entries/op-apply-time-no-account)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (CAP-0046):

- H-C16: OperationResult.opNO_ACCOUNT in a closed ledger: operation source merged earlier in the ledger

## The shape

Core applies a ledger's classic phase before its Soroban phase and re-checks the source account, sequence number, signatures and sequence-age preconditions at apply (TransactionFrame::commonValid; OperationFrame::checkSignature with forApply). Here a classic transaction earlier in the same ledger merges this transaction's operation source account away, so the transaction fails with txFAILED and the operation result opNO_ACCOUNT.

## Variants

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| [`p28-mainnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/op.apply-time.no-account/p28-mainnet-generated.xdr) | P28 | mainnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0 | 17,228 B | `b464fb610c5dc4338e51264688075287b17489787054fc0a9a3ed48926be972c` |

# The same classic payment under three node-flag profiles (/docs/corpus/entries/profiles-classic-payment-meta-by-flags)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (CAP-0067):

- H-F9: same ledger, three emitter-flag profiles
- H-F7: LedgerCloseMetaExt v1 under base and galexie flags, v0 under bare

## The shape

The same ledger as written by a node with base flags, with Galexie's six flags, and with none. The ledger is identical; the metadata is not: with no flags the classic transfer event and the fee events are absent and LedgerCloseMeta has no ext v1.

# With diagnostic events on, every contract event appears twice (/docs/corpus/entries/profiles-galexie-diagnostic-double-emission)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (CAP-0067):

- H-E3: contract event repeated in diagnostic_events
- H-F9: diagnostic events only under the galexie profile

## The shape

Galexie's default flags include ENABLE_SOROBAN_DIAGNOSTIC_EVENTS. The put's contract event appears in the operation's events and again, type contract, among the diagnostic events; a core_metrics event invoke_time_nsecs carries wall-clock time, so the bytes differ between nodes. stellar-etl#452.

# Deauthorizing a trustline removes offers, redeems pool shares into claimable balances and deletes the pool (/docs/corpus/entries/revoke-cascade-offers-pool-shares)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (CAP-0035, CAP-0038):

- H-D9: revocation creates claimable balances from pool shares and removes offers
- H-C10: trustline fully deauthorized (flags 4: only the clawback bit)
- H-C8: pool entry removed by a revocation
- H-F6: a ledger whose change order differed in every one of 20 core runs; minority orderings ship as files

## The shape

SET_TRUST_LINE_FLAGS clears every authorization on mm's XPF trustline. Core removes mm's three XPF offers, redeems mm's pool shares into two claimable balances for mm (no CREATE_CLAIMABLE_BALANCE), removes the pool-share trustline and, mm being the last shareholder, the pool itself. Readers that only create balances and pools from their own operations miss all of it.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`p30-mainnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/revoke.cascade-offers-pool-shares/p30-mainnet-generated.xdr) | P30 | mainnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0; change order varies: 20 orderings in 20 runs | 4,672 B | `02f5b6e95f4314b836a9319cbc5d8083b3350bf95618ff70ce8030c3b98d908d` |
| [`p30-testnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/revoke.cascade-offers-pool-shares/p30-testnet-generated.xdr) | P30 | testnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0; change order varies: 2 orderings in 2 runs | 4,672 B | `4875825271f25added5f632c2798bc635717b2dc997d78a348dd71498f0454e6` |

# A SAC balance held by a contract above int64 (/docs/corpus/entries/sac-contract-balance-above-int64)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (CAP-0046):

- H-B4: SAC contract balance i128 above int64
- H-B3: token amount above int64 max

The issuer mints 2^64 + 2^63 XPF to a contract. Contract balances in a SAC are i128 with no int64 cap, unlike trustlines. Readers that store token balances as int64 overflow.

# SAC trustline with no event (/docs/corpus/entries/sac-trust-creates-trustline)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (CAP-0073):

- H-D1: InvokeHostFunctionOp → LedgerEntryChange.created.TrustLineEntry (no operation event)

## The shape

Since CAP-0073 a contract call (the Stellar Asset Contract's `trust` function) can create a classic trustline. The trustline appears only as a created ledger entry in the operation's changes: there is no CHANGE_TRUST operation and no operation event. Readers that learn about trustlines from operation types or events drop it. wallet-backend recorded the balance but no TRUSTLINE/ADD state change (#731).

## Variants

The variants are **generated** by a standalone stellar-core v30.0.0 at protocols 30 and 28. On most of them the order of the operation's changes is not stable between core processes, so those pin an order-normalised hash and list every raw ordering seen.

| Variant | Protocol | Network | Source | Size | sha256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`p30-mainnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/sac.trust.creates-trustline/p30-mainnet-generated.xdr) | P30 | mainnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0; change order varies: 2 orderings in 20 runs | 2,924 B | `a08d8c7b8db5f37d1df6edc104b17cd6a7b024ceef30e70715a034454c3aabde` |
| [`p28-mainnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/sac.trust.creates-trustline/p28-mainnet-generated.xdr) | P28 | mainnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0; change order varies: 2 orderings in 2 runs | 2,916 B | `86051026e6f0ab0ea2c3dc3f2ef8da061b0a333f4bdd9a20c5cab0f0bf812628` |
| [`p30-testnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/sac.trust.creates-trustline/p30-testnet-generated.xdr) | P30 | testnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0 | 2,924 B | `4bd94c7a2455d6391b5fd5b6c5cd4267500a82c15719552ee1a0efb2b0b58f92` |
| [`p28-testnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/sac.trust.creates-trustline/p28-testnet-generated.xdr) | P28 | testnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0; change order varies: 2 orderings in 2 runs | 2,916 B | `a37deedf9fdec2914e6aab26259b19a0d02171ecffa39b8d363219fabbad82cf` |

Build `c152783c`, "record SAC-created trustline state changes" (#734, the fix for #731), records it. See [Replay](/docs/tools/replay).

# Map keys that collide (/docs/corpus/entries/scval-map-keys-collide-on-native-conversion)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (CAP-0046):

- H-B2: ContractDataEntry.val, ContractEvent.body.data, SorobanTransactionMeta.returnValue

## The shape

An ScMap may hold keys of different types that print the same: u32 1, i32 1, u64 1, the string "1" and the symbol "1" are five distinct, correctly ordered keys on chain. Converting the map to a native object keyed by text collapses them. js-stellar-sdk's scValToNative silently kept one of them (#1789). This entry is real stellar-core output: a contract wrote the map to storage, returned it and emitted it in an event.

The five keys are u32 1, i32 1, u64 1, the string "1" and the symbol 1. Each maps to a different value (10, 20, 30, 40, 50), so a conversion that drops entries is easy to detect.

## Variants

| Variant | Protocol | Network | Source | Size | sha256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`p30-mainnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/scval.map.keys-collide-on-native-conversion/p30-mainnet-generated.xdr) | P30 | mainnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0 | 2,972 B | `744986731d9719b9e03dceb25bef7e56aa2855ce08173c19b7da261d1531cb41` |
| [`p28-mainnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/scval.map.keys-collide-on-native-conversion/p28-mainnet-generated.xdr) | P28 | mainnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0 | 2,964 B | `6d54aaf35a75e1773e0b7789695da45933136ad0340f6ff013309284a7727600` |
| [`p30-testnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/scval.map.keys-collide-on-native-conversion/p30-testnet-generated.xdr) | P30 | testnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0 | 2,972 B | `a70bc215e80662a703b2077d59ddf90e8b5bdf41b17929f2719a6e9ea28cc3e7` |
| [`p28-testnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/scval.map.keys-collide-on-native-conversion/p28-testnet-generated.xdr) | P28 | testnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0 | 2,964 B | `46fed2036c0f50547b2172489ef7b8a29dd2e6c866c6d772c9d25c9ce05580c9` |

## What a correct reader returns

This entry has an **SDK check** (1 of 263 entries do). It is a rule for the SDK's own helper, not a value: keep all five entries, or refuse the map. Never return fewer.

<Callout title="Not run yet">The schema says SDK checks belong to the conformance runner, but no tool runs them yet. Today the runner uses its own vectors, below.</Callout>

| A correct reader finds | Value | Backed by |
|---|---|---|
| The contract wrote a persistent entry keyed `collide` whose value is a 5-entry map with keys u32 1, i32 1, u64 1, string "1", symbol "1" (in core's order). | some change where 7 fields match | construction, snapshot, core, walker |
| The event emitted by the call carries the same map with all 5 entries. | length `5` | construction, snapshot |
| The return value is the same 5-entry map. | length `5` | construction, snapshot |
| Each key maps to a different value (10, 20, 30, 40, 50), so a lossy conversion is detectable. | `50` | construction, snapshot, core, walker |

| SDK check | Must |
|---|---|
| Native projection of the event's map keeps all five entries or rejects the map; it never silently drops one. | return 5 entries, or raise an error; returning fewer than 5 is a failure (js-stellar-sdk#1789) |

## What it reproduces

[js-stellar-sdk#1789](https://github.com/stellar/js-stellar-sdk/issues/1789)

`make conformance` runs a vector with the same kind of collision (a two-entry map whose keys both read as "1") through js-stellar-sdk builds before and after the fix. The [recorded matrix](/docs/tools/conformance) shows 17.2.0 and 17.2.1 keeping 1 of 2 entries, and 17.3.0 rejecting the map.

## Check it yourself

```bash
make verify
make conformance
```

# Signed-payload signer (/docs/corpus/entries/signer-signed-payload-set-options)

Figure: the 44-byte signed-payload SignerKey from testnet ledger 4437357: type 3, a 32-byte ed25519 key, length 3, payload `de ad be`, and one byte of padding.

## The shape

CAP-0040 added a signer type that carries a payload: the strkey starts with P and is longer than a G address (up to 165 characters for a 64-byte payload). Readers that assume every signer is a 32-byte ed25519 key truncate it or fail. wallet-backend halted ingestion on testnet ledger 4437357 (#729) and stored the signer as 33 bytes, losing the payload (#716).

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (CAP-0040):

- H-A3: SetOptionsOp.signer.key (SIGNER_KEY_TYPE_ED25519_SIGNED_PAYLOAD)

## Variants

One variant is **mined**: the real testnet ledger where wallet-backend halted. Two are **generated** by a standalone stellar-core v30.0.0, on the mainnet and testnet passphrases. The generated ones push the edges: a 64-byte payload (the longest allowed, a 165-character strkey), and a 29-byte payload that needs XDR padding.

| Variant | Protocol | Network | Source | Size | sha256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`p30-mainnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/signer.signed-payload.set-options/p30-mainnet-generated.xdr) | P30 | mainnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0 | 2,904 B | `c3bc44b52a51e96c69503d0f458610ace17863940f43d0a594d49c3476aad88b` |
| [`p30-testnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/signer.signed-payload.set-options/p30-testnet-generated.xdr) | P30 | testnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0 | 2,904 B | `9a22f13104ed4400d439550e33cd775270a9916befdfeeb9d2dbaab352677745` |
| [`p28-testnet-mined`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/signer.signed-payload.set-options/p28-testnet-mined.xdr.zst) | P28 | testnet passphrase | mined from history | 58,256 B | `582e694b96bf69f894763909a1b058c1a2523d5634f2e0947393cee9765f4e0e` |

# A trapped mainnet call whose diagnostic events carry the contract's own error code (/docs/corpus/entries/soroban-contract-error-code-mainnet)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (CAP-0046):

# A trustline set to authorized-to-maintain-liabilities (/docs/corpus/entries/trustline-maintain-liabilities)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (CAP-0018, CAP-0035):

- H-C10: trustline flag AUTHORIZED_TO_MAINTAIN_LIABILITIES

## The shape

SET_TRUST_LINE_FLAGS clears AUTHORIZED (1) and sets AUTHORIZED_TO_MAINTAIN_LIABILITIES (2) on bob's XPF trustline, which also carries TRUSTLINE_CLAWBACK_ENABLED (4) inherited from the issuer: flags go from 5 to 6. # A transaction valid at submission fails at apply with txBAD_AUTH_EXTRA (/docs/corpus/entries/tx-apply-time-bad-auth-extra)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (CAP-0046):

- H-C16: TransactionResult.txBAD_AUTH_EXTRA at apply: a signature needed at submission is unused once the master weight rises

## The shape

u6 needs weight 2: its master key and s6 both sign, and both signatures are used at submission. A classic transaction earlier in the same ledger raises the master key's weight to 2. At apply core's signature checker stops once the master key meets the threshold (SignatureChecker.cpp), so s6's signature goes unused and the transaction fails with txBAD_AUTH_EXTRA. Readers that treat BAD_AUTH_EXTRA as a submission-only code meet it in a closed ledger.

# A transaction valid at submission fails txBAD_AUTH at apply (/docs/corpus/entries/tx-apply-time-bad-auth)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (CAP-0046):

- H-C16: TransactionResult.txBAD_AUTH in a closed ledger: signer removed earlier in the ledger

## The shape

Core applies a ledger's classic phase before its Soroban phase and re-checks the source account, sequence number, signatures and sequence-age preconditions at apply (TransactionFrame::commonValid; OperationFrame::checkSignature with forApply). Here a classic transaction earlier in the same ledger removes the only signer that signed this transaction, so it fails with txBAD_AUTH. Its sequence number is consumed and its fee charged.

# A transaction with minSeqLedgerGap fails at apply after a bump-to-0 in the same ledger (/docs/corpus/entries/tx-apply-time-bad-min-seq-age-or-gap)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (CAP-0021, CAP-0046):

- H-C16: TransactionResult.txBAD_MIN_SEQ_AGE_OR_GAP in a closed ledger: seqLedger moved earlier in the ledger

## The shape

Core applies a ledger's classic phase before its Soroban phase and re-checks the source account, sequence number, signatures and sequence-age preconditions at apply (TransactionFrame::commonValid; OperationFrame::checkSignature with forApply). Here a classic transaction earlier in the same ledger runs BUMP_SEQUENCE with bumpTo 0 on the source: the sequence number does not change, but seqLedger moves to this ledger (BumpSequenceOpFrame.cpp maybeUpdateAccountOnLedgerSeqUpdate), so this transaction's minSeqLedgerGap of 1 is no longer met and it fails with txBAD_MIN_SEQ_AGE_OR_GAP.

## Variants

| Variant | Protocol | Network | Source | Size | sha256 |

# A transaction valid at submission fails txBAD_SEQ at apply (/docs/corpus/entries/tx-apply-time-bad-seq)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (CAP-0046):

- H-C16: TransactionResult.txBAD_SEQ in a closed ledger: source sequence bumped earlier in the ledger

## The shape

Core applies a ledger's classic phase before its Soroban phase and re-checks the source account, sequence number, signatures and sequence-age preconditions at apply (TransactionFrame::commonValid; OperationFrame::checkSignature with forApply). Here a classic transaction earlier in the same ledger bumps the source account's sequence number, so this Soroban transaction fails with txBAD_SEQ. Its fee is charged and its sequence number is not consumed (tx_changes_before is empty). Readers that assume txBAD_SEQ never reaches a ledger, or that every failed transaction consumed a sequence number, get this wrong.

# A fee bump whose inner transaction fails at apply with txBAD_AUTH_EXTRA (/docs/corpus/entries/tx-apply-time-inner-bad-auth-extra)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (CAP-0015, CAP-0046):

- H-C16: InnerTransactionResult.txBAD_AUTH_EXTRA at apply: the inner transaction carries two signatures both needed at submission; at apply the master key alone meets the raised weight, so the second goes unused (SignatureChecker stops at the needed weight)
- H-C2: txFEE_BUMP_INNER_FAILED with inner txBAD_AUTH_EXTRA

## The shape

The inner transaction was valid when queued; a classic transaction earlier in the same ledger changed its source, and core re-checks the source at apply (TransactionFrame::commonValid, processSignatures): the inner transaction carries two signatures both needed at submission; at apply the master key alone meets the raised weight, so the second goes unused (SignatureChecker stops at the needed weight). The outer result is txFEE_BUMP_INNER_FAILED with txBAD_AUTH_EXTRA inside; the fee source pays. Readers that expect inner results to carry only operation failures, or treat a queued transaction as valid, get it wrong.

# A fee bump whose inner transaction fails at apply with txBAD_SEQ (/docs/corpus/entries/tx-apply-time-inner-bad-seq)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (CAP-0015, CAP-0046):

- H-C16: InnerTransactionResult.txBAD_SEQ at apply: the inner source's sequence number was bumped earlier in the ledger
- H-C2: txFEE_BUMP_INNER_FAILED with inner txBAD_SEQ

## The shape

The inner transaction was valid when queued; a classic transaction earlier in the same ledger changed its source, and core re-checks the source at apply (TransactionFrame::commonValid, processSignatures): the inner source's sequence number was bumped earlier in the ledger. The outer result is txFEE_BUMP_INNER_FAILED with txBAD_SEQ inside; the fee source pays. Readers that expect inner results to carry only operation failures, or treat a queued transaction as valid, get it wrong.

# A Soroban transaction fails txNO_ACCOUNT at apply and its fee is never refunded (/docs/corpus/entries/tx-apply-time-no-account-fee-not-refunded)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (CAP-0046):

- H-C16: TransactionResult.txNO_ACCOUNT in a closed ledger: source merged earlier in the ledger
- H-C13: Soroban fee source merged before the refund: fee_charged is the full maximum, no refund change or event

## The shape

Core applies a ledger's classic phase before its Soroban phase and re-checks the source account, sequence number, signatures and sequence-age preconditions at apply (TransactionFrame::commonValid; OperationFrame::checkSignature with forApply). Here a classic transaction earlier in the same ledger merges the source account after its fee was charged, so this Soroban transaction fails with txNO_ACCOUNT. The refund has nowhere to go: there is no post-apply fee change and no refund event, and fee_charged is the full declared maximum (TransactionFrame.cpp:998-1001). Readers that compute the fee as charge minus refund, or expect a refund for every Soroban transaction, get it wrong.

## Variants

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`p30-mainnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/tx.apply-time.no-account-fee-not-refunded/p30-mainnet-generated.xdr) | P30 | mainnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0 | 17,236 B | `dbc26aa0d75267052a7b0ff3a399e6a5f1bd708bf51da7b88e10fce8e646ba9b` |
| [`p28-mainnet-generated`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/entries/tx.apply-time.no-account-fee-not-refunded/p28-mainnet-generated.xdr) | P28 | mainnet passphrase | generated by stellar-core v30.0.0 | 17,228 B | `b464fb610c5dc4338e51264688075287b17489787054fc0a9a3ed48926be972c` |

# A config-settings upgrade: Soroban transaction limit and three frozen trustlines (/docs/corpus/entries/upgrade-config-lanes-and-freeze)

Where it sits, inside `LedgerCloseMeta` (CAP-0046, CAP-0077):

- H-F10: LEDGER_UPGRADE_CONFIG updating contract_execution_lanes and frozen_ledger_keys
- H-D12: frozen-key list grown by a config upgrade

## The shape

LEDGER_UPGRADE_CONFIG with two settings in one set: contract_execution_lanes (ledgerMaxTxCount 2) and frozen_ledger_keys (three trustlines). The new values appear only in upgradesProcessing, after the ledger's transactions.

# The corpus (/docs/corpus)

**What it is.** The heart of XDRProof: real Stellar ledgers in their rarest valid shapes, each kept as the exact bytes stellar-core wrote, with the answers a correct reader must give.

**Why it matters.** Your code meets ordinary ledgers every day and these rarely, often for the first time in production. The corpus lets you meet them in a test.

263 entries · 634 variants · 78 hazards in the registry · 72 hazards covered so far

The corpus is a set of **entries**, plus [37 mined ledgers](/docs/corpus/mined) from the real networks. Each entry is one rare shape, such as a signed-payload signer or a trustline created by a contract call, kept as real `LedgerCloseMeta` bytes. Each entry also carries the facts a correct reader must find in those bytes.

Entries grow by purpose, not by volume. Each one names the [hazards](/docs/hazards) it targets, and where in the XDR they sit.

The full list, grouped by family, is on [All entries](/docs/corpus/entries); every entry has its own page.

## How an entry is built

<Steps>
<Step>

### Picked from the hazard registry

A hazard is a named way readers break, with its evidence: an upstream issue, a protocol rule or a measurement. An entry targets one or more hazards, and says where each sits in the XDR (its `placement`).

</Step>
<Step>

### Written in the catalog, compiled from real runs

The entry's intent and facts are written in its [catalog file](/docs/corpus/catalog). The compiler takes the bytes from a recipe run of a bare standalone stellar-core, or from a ledger **mined** from public history, and resolves every fact against them. A fact that doesn't hold fails the build. `make generate` re-runs every recipe twice from scratch and checks that every shipped generated variant is reproduced: the same bytes, or the same content in another change order.

</Step>
<Step>

### Facts, and what backs each one

Every expected value says what backs it: `construction` (the recipe set that value), `snapshot` (the SEP-0051 rendering by the pinned stellar-xdr crate), `core` (stellar-core's own decoder), `walker` (XDRProof's schema walker) or `review`. 737 of the 1,296 facts are also confirmed by both stellar-core's decoder and the schema walker; the **Backed by** column on each entry page shows exactly which.

</Step>
<Step>

### Verified on every change

`make verify` checks the schema, sizes and hashes, a byte-for-byte round trip through native rs-stellar-xdr, the focus transaction and every fact. `make oracle` checks that each fact's values also appear in what stellar-core's own decoder and the schema walker read.

</Step>
</Steps>

## Files

<Files>
  <Folder name="catalog" defaultOpen>
    <File name="<id>.json" />
  </Folder>
  <Folder name="entries" defaultOpen>
    <Folder name="<id>" defaultOpen>
      <File name="entry.json" />
      <File name="p30-mainnet-generated.xdr" />
      <File name="p28-testnet-generated.xdr" />
    </Folder>
  </Folder>
  <Folder name="mined/ledgers" />
  <File name="manifest.json" />
  <Folder name="schema/v1">
    <File name="entry.schema.json" />
  </Folder>
</Files>

`manifest.json` is generated from the entries, one row per variant. `make verify` fails if it is out of date.


# Mined ledgers (/docs/corpus/mined)

**What it is.** Real mainnet and testnet ledgers, downloaded from the public data lake with their hashes and the query that found them.

**Why it matters.** Some shapes only happen on a live network, such as eviction at the per-ledger cap or a validator vote. These are the real bytes, not a reconstruction.

37 ledgers · 47 shape records · 34 mainnet, 3 testnet · protocols P12 P22 P28 P29 P30

Some shapes only happen on a real network, and some are worth having as real network bytes. Examples:
- eviction at the per-ledger cap;
- validator settings votes;
- a mainnet freeze of ledger keys (CAP-0077);
- protocol-12 V0 envelopes;
- protocol-22 refunds;
- multi-stage parallel Soroban phases.

`mined/` holds those as real `LedgerCloseMeta`, fetched from SDF's public data lake and located with BigQuery over the public Hubble dataset. The queries are in `mined/queries/`.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `mined/ledgers/<network>-<seq>.lcm.xdr.zst` | One ledger, zstd-compressed. Its sha256 and size describe the decompressed bytes: the lake object minus its 12-byte batch header |
| `mined/index.json` | One record per shape found in a ledger: the lake URL, the stellar-core version that wrote it, how it was located, the findings with exact JSON paths, and why readers break on it |

`make verify` also runs `tools/mined-verify.mjs`. Every file must match its hash, round-trip byte for byte through native rs-stellar-xdr, and carry the recorded sequence and protocol. Every finding's transaction and JSON path must be present. `make coverage` reports the union arms these ledgers reach: **289 of 499**.

<Callout title="Network data, not entries">These ledgers were written by SDF's Galexie with its default flags, so their metadata differs from a default node's (see [Found while building](/docs/findings)). Most are not corpus entries: entries carry facts and hazards, and these carry findings. The [catalog](/docs/corpus/catalog) also compiles entries from them: 37 entries so far, built from 22 of these ledgers, the signed-payload signer among them.</Callout>

## Every mined shape

| Shape | Ledger | Why readers break |
|---|---|---|
| fee bump inner failed | [mainnet 65517511](https://aws-public-blockchain.s3.amazonaws.com/v1.1/stellar/ledgers/pubnet/FC18F9FF--65472000-65535999/FC184838--65517511.xdr.zst) (P29, 365 txs) | The outer result is txFEE_BUMP_INNER_FAILED and the real result (inner hash, inner code, per-op codes) sits one level down in InnerTransactionResultPair; readers that only look at the outer code or outer hash report the wrong hash, fee or success flag. |
| muxed accounts | [mainnet 65517507](https://aws-public-blockchain.s3.amazonaws.com/v1.1/stellar/ledgers/pubnet/FC18F9FF--65472000-65535999/FC18483C--65517507.xdr.zst) (P29, 409 txs) | M-addresses appear only in the envelope (operation source, payment destination); the meta shows the base G-account and the id moves to the event's to_muxed_id, so readers that key on 32-byte accounts truncate, drop the id or double-count the participant. |

# Recipes (/docs/corpus/recipes)

**What it is.** Small scripts that make a private, offline stellar-core produce each rare shape on demand.

**Why it matters.** A shape you can rebuild from scratch is one anyone can verify, and one that can be made again when the protocol changes.

A recipe is a Node script (using `@stellar/stellar-sdk` 17.4.0) that drives one fresh **standalone stellar-core** over its HTTP port:

- **Fixed seeds.** Every keypair is `sha256('xdrproof:' + name)`; the root account comes from the passphrase.
- **Fixed time.** Ledger n closes at `1767225600 + n × 30 days`.
- **No RPC, no simulation.** Transactions go straight to core's `tx` endpoint, and ledgers close with `manualclose`.
- **Ledger 2 is always the protocol upgrade,** and never an entry.

Core's metadata stream is split into one `ledger-NNN.xdr` file per ledger, plus `SHA256SUMS`. An entry is one of those ledgers, chosen because it holds a rare shape.

## The two recipe sets

| Set | Script | Ledgers | What it covers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Classic | `recipes/classic/gen.mjs` | 3–105, at protocol 30 | Basics (the signed-payload signers at ledger 6), a catalogue of operations, two failure suites, blueprint placements, maximum-length vectors, a revocation cascade, surge pricing, and a final base-fee, set-size and ledger-flags upgrade |
| Soroban | `recipes/soroban/gen/gen.mjs` | 3–94 at P30 | Blueprint placements, apply-time failures, fee-bump inner failures, forged and V2-rendered auth signatures, two test contracts, delegated custom accounts, external-ref executables, config upgrades, frozen keys, eviction and automatic restore |

Entries are compiled from recipe steps (and mined ledgers) by the [catalog](/docs/corpus/catalog): 263 so far. The [hazard registry](/docs/hazards) references recipe ledgers by number.

## The test contracts

| Contract | SDK | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `xdrproof-kit` | soroban-sdk 25.3.0 | `put(k, v)` stores a value, emits it and returns it; `nest` builds authorization trees of any depth |
| `xdrproof-kit2` | soroban-sdk 28.0.0 | A constructor, persistent, temporary and instance storage, CAP-0085 executable references, and a `__check_auth` that delegates (CAP-0071) |

Both ship as prebuilt Wasm next to their source.

## How they are run

Each run starts the `stellar/quickstart` image pinned by digest in `recipes/core-image`, and refuses anything but stellar-core v30.0.0. The core config sets manual close, a fixed node seed, and one **emitter-flag profile** from `recipes/flags/`:

| Profile | Flags set | Who runs this way |
|---|---|---|
| `base` | `EMIT_CLASSIC_EVENTS`, `EMIT_SOROBAN_TRANSACTION_META_EXT_V1`, `EMIT_LEDGER_CLOSE_META_EXT_V1` | the corpus's shipped variants |
| `galexie` | all six: the three above plus `BACKFILL_STELLAR_ASSET_EVENTS`, `BACKFILL_RESTORE_META`, `ENABLE_SOROBAN_DIAGNOSTIC_EVENTS` | Galexie's default config, which public data lakes are written with |
| `bare` | none | a node on stellar-core's example config |

Soroban runs also set `TESTING_SOROBAN_HIGH_LIMIT_OVERRIDE`. Variant keys carry the profile as a suffix when it is not `base`.

`make generate` runs 10 configurations twice each: classic P30 on both passphrases, Soroban P30 and P28 on both passphrases, and the galexie and bare profiles at P30 mainnet for each lane. It checks that every shipped generated variant is reproduced. See [Generate](/docs/tools/generate).


# Manifest schema (/docs/corpus/schema)

**What it is.** The format of an entry, field by field, as a JSON Schema.

**Why it matters.** Any tool, in any language, can load the corpus and know what each field means without reading XDRProof's code.

The schema is [`schema/v1/entry.schema.json`](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/schema/v1/entry.schema.json), version 1.1. Every table on this page is generated from it.

## The RFP's fields

| RFP field | Schema |
|---|---|
| Entry ID | `id` + `variants[].key` (permanent; never reused) |
| CAP | `caps` |
| Protocol version | `variants[].protocol` |
| Source | `variants[].source`: `mined` with the lake URL and sha256, or `generated` with the core version, emitter flags and recipe |
| Synthetic flag | `variants[].synthetic` (with `emittable` when true) |
| Expected decoded values | `expected.facts` (order-independent where needed) and `expected.sdk_checks` |

Beyond those, each entry names its `hazards` (with the `placement` in the XDR), and each variant its `focus` transaction. Variants may be zstd-compressed (large mainnet ledgers); `size` and `sha256` describe the decompressed bytes.

## Entry

The entry schema: [schema/v1/entry.schema.json](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/schema/v1/entry.schema.json).

## Variant

One ledger file of an entry: a protocol, a network passphrase, and how it was obtained.

The `variant` definition schema: [schema/v1/entry.schema.json](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/schema/v1/entry.schema.json).

## Fact

One value a correct reader must find, at a path in the SEP-0051 JSON rendering. It is given as `equals`, `length` or `some` (a change that matches, in any order).

The `fact` definition schema: [schema/v1/entry.schema.json](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/schema/v1/entry.schema.json).

## SDK check

A rule for an SDK helper rather than a value. For example, a native projection must keep every entry of a map or refuse it.

The `sdk_check` definition schema: [schema/v1/entry.schema.json](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/schema/v1/entry.schema.json).


# Found while building (/docs/findings)

**What it is.** What building the corpus measured about stellar-core and the decoders: things the documentation doesn't say.

**Why it matters.** Each one is a trap for anyone reading the ledger, and each is now a test in the corpus.

Each finding says where it comes from: a committed measurement, a mined ledger, or an observation on recipe runs. The recipe runs themselves are not shipped. The recipes are, along with the order-scan and flag-profile results.

## stellar-core emits some operation changes in a random order

Across 20 fresh runs of each recipe lane, 33 of 103 classic recipe ledgers and 16 of 92 Soroban ones came out in more than one byte order (the protocol-upgrade ledger aside, which varies too). Their headers and content were identical. 5 classic ledgers (12, 14, 78, 80, 84) had a different order in every run. The cause is hash-map iteration with a per-process random salt. Measured by [`make order-scan`](/docs/tools/order-scan); the results are committed in `recipes/*/order-scan/`.

<Callout type="warn" title="For indexers">Never depend on the order of changes within an operation.</Callout>

## Node flags change the metadata, never the ledger

The recipes were run under the three [flag profiles](/docs/corpus/recipes) (base, Galexie and bare). Every ledger of both lanes keeps the same header hash.

- **Bare** changes the metadata content of every ledger except the protocol-upgrade one. There are no classic events, no fee events, and v0 meta extensions.
- **Galexie's** extra flags change no classic ledger, and 46 Soroban ones: every ledger with a contract call. In those, each contract event appears twice, in the operation's events and again among the diagnostic events.

[`make generate`](/docs/tools/generate) re-measures this into `recipes/<lane>/profiles/`.

## A Soroban ledger written with diagnostic events on is not byte-reproducible

Every call carries a `core_metrics` diagnostic event, `invoke_time_nsecs`: the wall-clock time the host spent. Two nodes running Galexie's default config write different bytes for the same ledger. The corpus's normalised form zeroes that one value.

## The public data lake carries TransactionMeta v4, even for 2019 ledgers

Every lake object inspected, at protocols 12, 22 and 29, has v4 meta. The protocol-12 mainnet ledger in [`mined/`](/docs/corpus/mined) has v4 meta and 532 V0 envelopes. This is because Galexie sets `BACKFILL_STELLAR_ASSET_EVENTS`, which makes stellar-core write v4 at any protocol. A default node replaying the same ledger writes v2 (v3 for protocols 20–22). Only the `LedgerCloseMeta` arm varies by era: v0 at protocol 12, v1 at 22, v2 at 29.

## A Soroban fee source merged earlier in the same ledger gets no refund

`fee_charged` is then the full declared maximum, with no refund change and no refund event. A reader that computes the fee as the charge minus the refund, or that expects a refund for every Soroban transaction, gets it wrong.

## stellar-core's own golden ledgers reach 254 of 499 arms

A `LedgerCloseMeta` reader can meet 499 XDR union arms at v30.0. stellar-core's own golden ledger files reach 254 of them. For comparison, the corpus entries reach 417 and the mined ledgers 289 ([Coverage](/docs/tools/coverage)). Many of the missing arms are result codes that never appear in a closed ledger. Measured by [`make coverage-goldens`](/docs/tools/coverage) against stellar-core commit `f2b91947`.

## Soroban authorization trees apply up to 245 levels deep

At Protocol 30, an authorization tree 245 levels deep applies. At 246 the transaction is included, but traps. Any indexer cap below about 246 meets real, valid ledgers. Re-checked by `make verify` on the entries [`auth.tree-depth-245-max`](/docs/corpus/entries/auth-tree-depth-245-max) and [`auth.tree-depth-246-trapped`](/docs/corpus/entries/auth-tree-depth-246-trapped).

## The WASM build of rs-stellar-xdr cannot decode those ledgers

`@stellar/stellar-xdr-json` 30.0.0, rs-stellar-xdr compiled to WASM, refuses 13 corpus variants that stellar-core wrote (`depth limit exceeded`): 8 whose authorization tree is 245 levels deep, the deepest that applies, and 5 at 246, which core includes and traps. The package hard-codes `XDR_MAX_DEPTH = 500`, set to mirror the Soroban host's budget limit, and applies it to the whole `LedgerCloseMeta`, whose path down to the auth tree is deeper. js-stellar-sdk 17.4.0, go-stellar-sdk v0.9.0, both Python decoders and native rs-stellar-xdr read them. This is finding F-1, reported as [js-stellar-xdr-json#67](https://github.com/stellar/js-stellar-xdr-json/issues/67); see [Reported upstream](/docs/findings/reported).

Figure (animated): how deep is too deep. Counted from the authorization entry, as stellar-core counts, the deepest tree it applies needs depth 499, under the limit of 500. Counted from the transaction it needs 507, and from the ledger 519; @stellar/stellar-xdr-json counts from the ledger and refuses it.

## A create-contract authorization is signed over bytes it does not contain

A valid v1 create-contract authorization is signed over its V2 rendering. The host reads `SOROBAN_AUTHORIZED_FUNCTION_TYPE_CREATE_CONTRACT_HOST_FN` into its V2 form and hashes the signature payload from the `CREATE_CONTRACT_V2_HOST_FN` rendering (soroban-env-host `auth.rs`, as stellar-core v30 links it at protocols 28 and 30). Signed over its own bytes, as js-stellar-base's `authorizeEntry` signs it, the entry fails ed25519 verification; signed over the V2 rendering, the contract is created.

This is by design since protocol 22, to keep one valid payload per action ([stellar discussion #1501](https://github.com/orgs/stellar/discussions/1501)). Transactions built through RPC simulation get it right; offline signers must sign the V2 rendering. A verifier that recomputes the payload from the entry rejects a signature core accepted (hazard [H-B16](/docs/hazards/layer-b#h-b16)). `tools/auth-payload-check.mjs` re-checks it with hand-encoded preimages, no SDK.

## Codes read as submission-only appear in closed ledgers

Core re-checks sequence numbers, signatures and preconditions at apply. So a classic transaction earlier in the same ledger can make a queued Soroban transaction fail with `txBAD_AUTH_EXTRA` (a signature needed at submission becomes surplus once a master weight rises), and fee-bump inner transactions fail with `txBAD_SEQ`, `txNO_ACCOUNT`, `txBAD_AUTH`, `txBAD_AUTH_EXTRA` or `txBAD_MIN_SEQ_AGE_OR_GAP` inside `txFEE_BUMP_INNER_FAILED`. The corpus's failed-transaction family holds them.

## Order across ledger keys is unstable; the pairing for one key is stable

Between core processes, the order across different ledger keys changes. The STATE → UPDATED pairing for one key does not. Readers can rely on the pairing, never on the order between keys.


# Reported upstream (/docs/findings/reported)

**What it is.** Two bugs XDRProof found in other projects' code that nobody had reported, filed upstream; a tested fix offered on an issue that was already open; and evidence added to another team's own report.

**Why it matters.** A test kit earns trust by what it catches. Each report below comes with a figure, a reproduction anyone can run, and, where we could, a tested fix. Filing is done the way the projects ask: a duplicate search first, one issue per bug.

## F-3: balances stored short on protocol 20–22 ledgers

Reported: [stellar/wallet-backend#834](https://github.com/stellar/wallet-backend/issues/834) · fix: [fix/pre-p23-soroban-refund-balances](https://github.com/Blockchain-Oracle/wallet-backend/compare/main...fix/pre-p23-soroban-refund-balances)

![Before protocol 23, each Soroban fee refund sits inside its own transaction's changes, which wallet-backend does not read; from protocol 23 all refunds come in one block it does read. On pubnet ledger 56085459, 7 of 7 refunded accounts are stored short.](https://xdrproof.dev/findings/f3-refunds.png)

![A terminal: the replay harness runs the protocol 22 ledger into wallet-backend main and reports it mishandled; a jq query lists the seven accounts, each stored short by its refund.](https://xdrproof.dev/findings/f3-repro.gif)

Before protocol 23, stellar-core credits a Soroban fee refund inside the transaction's own changes. wallet-backend builds native balances from fees, operations and the newer, separate refund block only, so every refunded account on such a ledger is stored short by exactly its refund, while wallet-backend's own balance history adds up.

It bites when an indexer works through older ledgers, such as a catch-up from the data lake. The fix is on a branch; the whole corpus replayed into it handles both variants of that ledger and changes no other verdict.


## F-1: a decoder refuses a ledger stellar-core closed

Reported: [stellar/js-stellar-xdr-json#67](https://github.com/stellar/js-stellar-xdr-json/issues/67)

![Bars for one transaction with a 245-deep authorization tree: the authorization entry needs depth 499, which fits the limit of 500; the transaction needs 507 and the ledger 519, both refused.](https://xdrproof.dev/findings/f1-depth.png)

![A terminal: a corpus ledger is downloaded and decoded with @stellar/stellar-xdr-json 30.0.0, which fails with depth limit exceeded.](https://xdrproof.dev/findings/f1-repro.gif)

`@stellar/stellar-xdr-json` 30.0.0, the WebAssembly build of rs-stellar-xdr, limits nesting to 500 levels for the whole value it decodes. stellar-core allows 500 per authorization entry, and the layers around a transaction add more, so the deepest trees core applies cannot be decoded once they are inside a transaction or a ledger. The corpus made them on a standalone stellar-core v30.0.0 with Soroban's resource limits raised for testing (`TESTING_SOROBAN_HIGH_LIMIT_OVERRIDE`), which the entry records.

It refuses 13 corpus variants that stellar-core wrote. Every other decoder tested reads them; see [Conformance](/docs/tools/conformance).


Figure (animated): how deep is too deep. Counted from the authorization entry, as stellar-core counts, the deepest tree it applies needs depth 499, under the limit of 500. Counted from the transaction it needs 507, and from the ledger 519; @stellar/stellar-xdr-json counts from the ledger and refuses it.

## wallet-backend#820: an authorization walk with no limit

Reported: [fix offered · wallet-backend#820](https://github.com/stellar/wallet-backend/issues/820#issuecomment-7009772300)

![A 245-deep chain of invocations with a bound drawn at depth 256. A limit that returns an error halts ingestion on every retry; the proposed limit stops descending, counts and logs, and the ledger ingests.](https://xdrproof.dev/findings/820-bounded-walk.png)

wallet-backend walks the authorization tree a transaction declares with no depth or node limit (issue #820, filed by another team). [The linter](/docs/tools/linter) finds it as `XP002/walk-unbudgeted`.

The fix offered bounds the walk well above anything the network applies today, and stops at the limit instead of failing. Our first version failed at depth 64, which would have halted ingestion on the 245-deep ledgers in the corpus; that mistake is now a linter rule of its own, `XP002/budget-fails`.

When one SDK fails a corpus entry, the same entry goes through the others. For F-1, java-stellar-sdk 6.0.0 refuses the same 13 ledgers at its default decoding depth; with a higher limit, every one decodes and round-trips.

# Upstream bugs (/docs/findings/reproduced)

**What it is.** Real bugs that other teams found in wallet-backend and the SDKs, reproduced from corpus ledgers and test vectors.

**Why it matters.** Each one is pinned. If a fix regresses, or an old bug turns up in another SDK, the run fails.

Verdicts come from state, never from log text: the indexer's cursor, process and stored rows for replay, the value returned for conformance. Every row below is pinned in `replay/expectations/` or `conformance/expectations/`, so a fix upstream shows up as an unexpected pass and the row is updated. The full triage is [findings/REPORT.md](https://github.com/XDRProof/xdrproof/blob/main/findings/REPORT.md).
